We need to write formative feedback as JSON. Address student as "you". Be specific, supportive, actionable. Cite sections/figures. Name what they did well, state what next rubric level requires. Don't change marks. Don't comment on conversion artefacts. Don't make up explanations for unclear reasoning.

Summary: acknowledge strengths: clear mission concept, rationale, single satellite justification, structured report, STK screenshots, launch/orbit/ground/EOL coverage. Main issues: SSO inclination 87.79 vs ~97.8, Kourou latitude 45.05 vs ~5.2, contact duration overstatement, missing link/swath, missing STK files, referencing. Keep <=80 words.

Next steps: 3 actionable. E.g. 1) Correct orbital geometry: recompute SSO inclination for 600 km (~97.8° retrograde), fix Kourou latitude, re-run STK and update text/table/figure consistency; include GSD/swath calculation. 2) Add quantitative comms/link budget and contact analysis: reconcile mean contact (~9.7 min) with text, include data rate/link margin and ground station capability; support EOL with deorbit lifetime/ballistic coefficient and debris compliance. 3) Improve evidence/referencing: include STK/PIGI files in appendix, number/caption all figures/tables, replace Wikipedia and ensure all citations [49]-[74] appear in reference list; explicitly define operator/customers and strengthen conclusion with EOL/quant results.

Criteria:
C1 <=70 words: You clearly explain mission need and single-satellite rationale with references. To reach Accomplished, explicitly identify operator and customers (not just implicit Australian facilities/UTAS/scientists), add detailed user/operations discussion, and use quality literature rather than bare URLs. Keep the strong rationale.

C2 <=70 words: You cover launch, orbit, ground control, duration and EOL with STK screenshots. Next level requires correcting SSO inclination (~97.8° not 87.79°), Kourou latitude (~5.2°N), and contact duration (~9.7 min mean); adding GSD/swath and link-budget calculations; including STK files; and supporting drag-sail EOL with deorbit-lifetime/compliance evidence.

C3 <=70 words: Your conclusion restates launch, orbit and ground station choices. To reach Accomplished, include key quantitative outcomes (altitude, inclination, contact stats, mission lifetime), state EOL approach, and avoid overclaiming a fully described configuration. Tie conclusions directly to evidence in the main body.

C4 <=70 words: Structure, headings and executive summary are clear. Next level requires numbered/captioned figures and tables, consistent formatting, and a reference list that matches all in-text citations (including [49]-[74]); replace Wikipedia with credible sources and proofread grammar. This will make the report professional and easy to follow.
